title: Flag Days: Good Luck, True South

sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐秘。

sentences.en: Let me be the first to wish you a happy Flag Day.
sentences.zh: 让我成为第一个祝大家国旗日快乐的人。

sentences.en: I assume I'm the firSt. I'm probably the only person to wish you a happy Flag Day.
sentences.zh: 我想我是第一个。我大概也是唯一一个祝大家国旗日快乐的人。

sentences.en: For those of you beautiful nerds who weren't aware, Flag Day is June 14th, so consider this your advance notice.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不知道的可爱极客们，国旗日是6月14日，所以提前通知你们一声。

sentences.en: If you haven't hoisted your favorite flag on your halyard up to the truck or finial of your flagpole
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有把最喜欢的国旗挂在旗绳上，升到旗杆顶端或顶饰处

sentences.en: to admire its field and canton and watch the fly-in wave in the wind,
sentences.zh: 去欣赏它的旗地和 canton，看着它在风中飘扬

sentences.en: Anyone who's listened to 99% Invisible regularly or seen my TED talk about flags
sentences.zh: 任何经常收听《99% Invisible》或看过我关于国旗的 TED 演讲的人

sentences.en: knows that we here at 99PI, we have a thing for flags.
sentences.zh: 都知道我们 99PI 的人对国旗有着特殊的情结。

sentences.en: Our stories have helped inspire people around the world to design and submit dozens of new flags
sentences.zh: 我们的故事曾激励世界各地的人们设计并向
地方和州政府提交了数十面新旗帜。

sentences.en: Flags can be beautiful things that give communities something symbolic to rally around.
sentences.zh: 国旗可以是美好的事物，能为社区提供凝聚共识的象征。

sentences.en: They can also be divisive and horrible.
sentences.zh: 它们也可能充满争议、丑陋不堪。

sentences.en: But since the beginning of this show, I've always liked using them as a way to talk about our lives as humans.
sentences.zh: 但从这个节目开播以来，我一直喜欢用它们作为探讨人类生活的切入点。

sentences.en: And this year, we decided to get the Flag Day celebration started early
sentences.zh: 今年，我们决定提前开启国旗日的庆祝活动

sentences.en: and then keep the party going with two whole weeks of flag-related stories.
sentences.zh: 然后用整整两周与国旗相关的故事将狂欢延续下去。

sentences.en: Before we dive in, though, let's take a brief look at the history of the most popular flag in the country,
sentences.zh: 不过在深入探讨之前，让我们先简要回顾一下国内最受欢迎的国旗的历史，

sentences.en: which is, of course, the flag of the country.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就是国家的国旗。

sentences.en: The flag United States of America is everywhere in this country,
sentences.zh: 美利坚合众国的国旗在这个国家的无处不在，

sentences.en: Stars and Stripes haven't always held such a lofty position in popular culture.
sentences.zh: 星条旗在流行文化中并非一直享有如此崇高的地位。

sentences.en: For much of American history, flags were more utilitarian, used to signal federal or military locations.
sentences.zh: 在大部分美国历史中，国旗更具实用性，用于标示联邦或军事地点。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the Civil War that everyday flag usage really got off the ground.
sentences.zh: 直到南北战争，日常国旗的使用才真正普及开来。

sentences.en: In 1861, when Confederates attacked Fort Sumter in Charleston,
sentences.zh: 1861年，当南方邦联军队进攻查尔斯顿的萨姆特堡时，

sentences.en: Union flags began showing up all over the North.
sentences.zh: 北方各地开始出现联邦国旗。

sentences.en: In the wake of the war, flags were increasingly incorporated into products, too,
sentences.zh: 战后，国旗也越来越多地被融入产品中，

sentences.en: going mainstream in an unprecedented way.
sentences.zh: 以史无前例的方式进入主流。

sentences.en: All of this patriotism helped lead to the establishment of an official Flag Day in 1916.
sentences.zh: 所有这些爱国主义情绪促成了1916年官方国旗日的设立。

sentences.en: So in my TED Talk and in past episodes, we've talked a lot about the design principles of flags,
sentences.zh: 所以在我的 TED 演讲和过往节目中，我们多次讨论过国旗的设计原则，

sentences.en: like what makes a good and bad city, state, and country flag.
sentences.zh: 比如什么构成了好与坏的城市、州和国家国旗。

sentences.en: But for Flag Day this year, and over the next couple of episodes,
sentences.zh: 但对于今年的国旗日，以及接下来的几期节目中，

sentences.en: we're going to talk about a few flags that are not tied directly to nation-states and municipalities.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论一些并非直接与民族国家和市镇挂钩的旗帜。

sentences.en: They're both bigger in scope than a country, but also more personal, too.
sentences.zh: 它们的范畴比国家更大，但也更加个人化。

sentences.en: So without further ado, up first is producer Joe Rosenberg.
sentences.zh: 闲话少说，首先登场的是制作人乔·罗森伯格。

sentences.en: So, Joe, I hear you have a really good flag story for me.
sentences.zh: 那么，乔，我听说你有一个非常棒的关于国旗的故事。

sentences.en: And it's a flag story, which is one I kind of came across really accidentally.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于国旗的故事，我其实是纯属偶然遇到的。

sentences.en: I was not trying to do work for 99PI.
sentences.zh: 我当时并不是在为 99PI 工作。

sentences.en: But no, what this story is, is a few years ago, a couple of friends and I in the Bay Area
sentences.zh: 不过说真的，这个故事是这样的：几年前，湾区我和几个朋友

sentences.en: ended up checking out this little museum, actually not that far from the 99PI offices,
sentences.zh: 顺道参观了这个小博物馆，其实离 99PI 办公室不远，

sentences.en: called the Alameda Naval Air Museum.
sentences.zh: 叫做阿拉米达海军航空博物馆。

sentences.en: And the Alameda Naval Air Museum is, how to put this?
sentences.zh: 而阿拉米达海军航空博物馆，怎么说呢？

sentences.en: Because it's one of those museums that is just kind of just made with love, right?
sentences.zh: 因为它就是那种充满爱意打造的博物馆，对吧？

sentences.en: It's literally my favorite kind of museum, like a little museum devoted to one thing that
sentences.zh: 这绝对是我最喜欢的博物馆类型，就像一个小博物馆只专注于一件事，

sentences.en: you can take in all at once.
I honestly like, I love museums like this.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我真的很喜欢这种博物馆。

sentences.en: And so it is a museum devoted to naval aviation history.
sentences.zh: 这是一个专门展示海军航空历史的博物馆。

sentences.en: And so it has display cases with medals and ship models and mannequins with uniforMs.
sentences.zh: 里面有陈列着勋章、舰船模型的展柜，还有穿着制服的人体模型。

sentences.en: There's like a DVD playing in a loop in one room.
sentences.zh: 某个房间里还在循环播放 DVD。

sentences.en: And so when my friends and I visited, we were, I admit, not planning to stay long.
sentences.zh: 所以当时我和朋友去参观时，坦白说，并没有打算待太久。

sentences.en: But then, just as we were about to leave, we came across this flag.
sentences.zh: 但就在我们准备离开时，我们偶然看到了这面旗帜。

sentences.en: And it wasn't even on display yet.
sentences.zh: 它当时甚至还没有被正式展出。

sentences.en: But on that day, it was kind of like in a frame on the floor, leaning against another display.
sentences.zh: 但在那天，它就像是被放在地板上的一个框里，靠在另一个展品旁边。

sentences.en: But the second we saw it, we were all just like riveted.
sentences.zh: 但我们一看到它，全都被它深深吸引住了。

sentences.en: And what it was, was a Japanese flag, but not your normal Japanese flag.
sentences.zh: 那是一面日本国旗，但不是普通的日本国旗。

sentences.en: Was it the rising sun flag with the rays coming out of it?
sentences.zh: 是带有光芒四射的旭日旗吗？

sentences.en: No, that's the Japanese military flag, of course, which is a whole other story.
sentences.zh: 不，那是日本军旗，当然，那是完全是另外一回事了。

sentences.en: No, this one was the regular Japanese national flag, also known as the Hinamaru.
sentences.zh: 不，这面是普通的日本国旗，也被称为日章旗（Hinamaru）。

sentences.en: But this is one with the red sun in the middle and the white field.
sentences.zh: 就是中间有红太阳、底色为白色的那种。

sentences.en: It's kind of what you'd think of as the flag of Japan.
sentences.zh: 这就是你通常会想到的日本国旗。

sentences.en: Except on this Hinamaru, the white part of the flag was just covered in writing.
sentences.zh: 只不过在这面日章旗上，旗帜白色的部分写满了字。

sentences.en: And so I did what any person would do, which is I took a picture.
sentences.zh: 所以我做了任何人都会做的事，那就是拍了张照片。

sentences.en: And here, let me show you that.
Okay, so all these phrases written in what looks like kanji, like kind of radiating out from the sun.
sentences.zh: 好吧，所有的这些短语都是用看起来像汉字的文字写的，就像是从太阳辐射出来的一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, and for the listeners who can't see it, this is not like a produced flag.
sentences.zh: 是的，对于看不到的听众来说，这不是那种量产的国旗。

sentences.en: Handwritten calligraphy consisting of many different messages in all different hands written directly on the fabric.
sentences.zh: 手写的书法包含了许多不同的讯息，出自不同人的手笔，直接写在织物上。

sentences.en: It seems as if maybe there's 50 or so people, maybe more, and they all have something written on it.
sentences.zh: 看起来大概有50人左右，甚至更多，每个人都在上面写了些东西。

sentences.en: And do you know what it says?
sentences.zh: 你知道上面写的是什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, because it just so happens that one of the friends I was with, she was Japanese.
sentences.zh: 嗯，知道，因为正好我同行的朋友中有一位是日本人。

sentences.en: Did she know what this was?
I mean, could she tell you more about this flag?
sentences.zh: 我是说，她能为你详细解读这面旗帜吗？

sentences.en: No, she didn't know what it was, but she started reading the flag aloud for us.
sentences.zh: 不，她一开始也不知道是什么，但她开始大声为我们朗读旗上的字。

sentences.en: Yeah, so along one side in the biggest characters was the name of a Japanese soldier from World War II to whom the flag presumably belonged,
sentences.zh: 好的，沿着一边最大的字是一位二战日本士兵的名字，这面旗帜显然属于他，

sentences.en: and who had appeared must have been going off to war.
sentences.zh: 他当时一定是去参军打仗了。

sentences.en: Because the messages around the sun were from people the flag bearer seemed to know who were giving him, like, this big send-off.
sentences.zh: 因为太阳周围的留言来自旗帜持有者认识的人，他们似乎在为他举行这种盛大的欢送。

sentences.en: And I'm not going to lie, some of them wrote rather strong statements.
sentences.zh: 我不会撒谎，其中有些人写的话相当激烈。

sentences.en: So the most explicit was, we have to kill British and Americans.
sentences.zh: 最直白的一句是：我们要杀光英美鬼子。

sentences.en: But then there were also lines that were just sad, knowing what this soldier and others were about to go through.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些话让人感到悲伤，一想到这位士兵和其他人即将经历的一切。

sentences.en: So, you know, there was, we hope you will protect our country, we have the strength to win, I hope we win this year.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，上面有：我们希望你保卫国家，我们有获胜的力量，我希望我们今年能赢。

sentences.en: And one person also wrote, like, I'm going to.
But honestly, the most common phrase was just, good luck.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，最常见的词还是：祝你好运。

sentences.en: Probably that was, like, a quarter to a third of the messages were just, good luck, or good luck this year.
sentences.zh: 大概有四分之一到三分之一的留言都只是“祝你好运”或“祝今年好运”。

sentences.en: Yeah, and it turns out that what we were looking at was something called, in Japanese, a yosagaki hinamaru, which means collection of writing around the sun.
sentences.zh: 是的，原来我们看到的是日语中所谓的“出征日章旗”（yosagaki hinamaru），意思是围绕太阳的文字集合。

sentences.en: But in English, it's known as a good luck flag.
sentences.zh: 但在英语中，它被称为幸运旗（good luck flag）。

sentences.en: And it was part of a tradition, very popular in Japan in the late 30s and early 40s, of having people write personal messages on flags to servicemen about to go off overseas.
sentences.zh: 这是30年代末和40年代初在日本非常流行的一个传统，人们在即将远赴海外的军人的旗帜上写下个人寄语。

sentences.en: And then they would actually carry this flag, fold it up on their person, into battle.
sentences.zh: 然后他们会把这面旗帜折叠好随身携带，带上战场。

sentences.en: And so, do we know exactly how this tradition of the good luck flag emerged?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们确切知道幸运旗这个传统是如何兴起的吗？

sentences.en: Boy, Joe, I have spent years and years trying to find that out.
sentences.zh: 天哪，乔，我花了整整好多年试图查明这一点。

sentences.en: Uh, so this is Rex Zeke.
sentences.zh: 呃，这位是雷克斯·齐克（Rex Zeke）。

sentences.en: He is a founder of an organization called Oban Society, which is involved with good luck flags.
sentences.zh: 他是一个名为“御盆协会”（Oban Society）的组织的创始人，该组织致力于处理幸运旗相关事务。

sentences.en: Uh, more on that in a second.
And he says most scholars chart the rise of these flags to the 1930s, when a lot of Japanese men were getting shipped off to fight in China.
sentences.zh: 他说，大多数学者将这些旗帜的兴起追溯到20世纪30年代，当时许多日本男子被派往中国作战。

sentences.en: But exactly how the tradition started, no one knows.
sentences.zh: 但这个传统究竟是如何开始的，没有人知道。

sentences.en: As far as I can tell, at some point, somebody got out a brush and some ink and they looked at their national flag and saw all that tempting white field all around that red area.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，在某个时刻，有人拿起了刷子和墨水，看着他们的国旗，看到了红色区域周围所有诱人的白色留白。

sentences.en: And this became a fashion or a tradition or it became instantly a thing and everybody started doing it.
sentences.zh: 这成了一种风尚、一种传统，或者说瞬间流行开来，每个人都开始这么做。

sentences.en: But one thing Rex really stressed, and I think this is very important to point out, is that most of these flags weren't nearly as militant as the one I saw in the museum.
sentences.zh: 但雷克斯强调的一点，我认为这一点非常重要，那就是这些旗帜大多数并不像我在博物馆里看到的那样充满好战情绪。

sentences.en: A lot of them do have messages about victory and country and being brave, but most of them were filled in with either just people's signatures and well wishes,
sentences.zh: 它们中的许多确实有关于胜利、国家和勇敢的留言，但大多数都填满了人们的签名和祝福，

sentences.en: or else these very intimate messages from loved ones and friends and neighbors.
sentences.zh: 或者是来自挚爱、朋友和邻居的非常亲密的留言。

sentences.en: Because you have to understand, you really could write almost anything.
sentences.zh: 因为你必须明白，你真的几乎可以写任何东西。

sentences.en: So there's no rules and regulation or, you know, there's no guidelines.
sentences.zh: 所以没有规章制度，或者说，没有任何准则。

sentences.en: And anybody might think, this is the last time to see this man.
sentences.zh: 任何人都会想：这可能是最后一次见到这个人了。

sentences.en: You may not ever see him again.
sentences.zh: 你可能再也见不到他了。
所以它是非常个人化的。

sentences.en: Keiko Zeke is Rex's partner and the co-founder of Obon Society.
sentences.zh: 凯科·齐克（Keiko Zeke）是雷克斯的伴侣兼御盆协会的联合创始人。

sentences.en: And she says people might sometimes put poetry on the flag, others put inside jokes, priests from the local temple might write a favorite mantra.
sentences.zh: 她说人们有时会在旗上写诗，其他人会写内部笑话，当地寺庙的僧侣可能会写下最喜欢的真言。

sentences.en: I remember one entry where it was saying something like, I'll look after the farm until you get home, or I'll look after the animals until you get home.
sentences.zh: 我记得有一条留言大致是：我会照顾农场直到你回家，或者我会照顾动物直到你回家。

sentences.en: So the soldier doesn't worry about at home while he's away.
sentences.zh: 这样士兵在外面时就不必担心家里的事情了。

sentences.en: I love that it can be anything.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢它可以是任何内容这一点。

sentences.en: And by the way, when Rex said everybody started doing it, he meant that more or less literally.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，当雷克斯说每个人都开始这么做时，他的意思是字面上的差不多。

sentences.en: We estimate that between like 1935 and 1945, the people of Japan created somewhere between 9 and 12 million of these flags.
sentences.zh: 我们估计在1935年到1945年之间，日本人民创作了大约900万到1200万面这样的旗帜。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons there's so many of them is not only did virtually every soldier get a flag, he often got multiple flags from multiple institutions on multiple occasions.
sentences.zh: 数量如此之多的原因之一不仅是几乎每个士兵都有一面旗帜，他通常还会在多个场合从多个机构获得多面旗帜。

sentences.en: And so he might go to war or leave home with one from his parents, one from the bank where he worked, and one from his baseball team.
sentences.zh: 所以他去参战或离家时可能会带着父母送的一面、工作银行送的一面，以及棒球队送的一面。

sentences.en: Okay, so if there's millions of these flags, you know, what happened to all of them?
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果有数百万面这样的旗帜，你知道，它们都怎么了？
比如说，它们现在在哪里？

sentences.en: Well, most of them are gone, at least in Japan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大部分都不见了，至少在日本是这样。

sentences.en: And that's because many of those soldiers never came home.
sentences.zh: 这是因为许多士兵再也没有回家。

sentences.en: So a lot of the flags were just lost forever.
sentences.zh: 所以很多旗帜就永远遗失了。

sentences.en: And many of the flags that did make it back to Japan might have been actually deliberately gotten rid of, because after the war during the American occupation,
sentences.zh: 许多好不容易回到日本的旗帜，可能实际上被故意处理掉了，因为在战后美军占领期间，

sentences.en: certain Japanese symbols were temporarily banned.
sentences.zh: 某些日本象征符号被临时禁止了。

sentences.en: And so those soldiers who survived, who had these and went home, whether those flags would have been buried or burned or destroyed or kept, we really can't get a gauge on that.
sentences.zh: 因此，那些生还并带着这些旗帜回家的士兵，这些旗帜是被埋了、烧了、毁了还是被保留下来，我们真的无法估计。

sentences.en: But Keiko says that the result is that it was such a final ending to this tradition, that most people in Japan today, if you show them one of these flags,
sentences.zh: 但凯科说，结果是这个传统迎来了如此彻底的终结，以至于今天日本的大多数人，如果你给他们看其中一面旗帜，

sentences.en: they don't know what it is.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道那是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah, they had no idea about Yosegaki no matter and anything.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们对日章旗一无所知，对什么都不知道。

sentences.en: But it turns out there is at least one country where you can still find a lot of good luck flags.
sentences.zh: 不过话又说回来，至少还有一个国家，你能在那儿找到大量的好运旗。

sentences.en: Okay, well, tell me where that is.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那告诉我这在哪个国家。

sentences.en: Well, it's kind of for an unsavory reason.
sentences.zh: 其实，原因有点不太光彩。

sentences.en: But basically, in World War II, a ton of American soldiers were shipped off to the Pacific and fought in battles against a ton of Japanese soldiers.
sentences.zh: 但基本上，在二战期间，大量的美国士兵被运往太平洋，并与大量的日本士兵进行了战斗。

sentences.en: And when the Americans took personal items off of dead Japanese soldiers on the battlefield, you have to understand,
sentences.zh: 当美国人在战场上从战死日本士兵身上拿走私人物品时，你必须明白，

sentences.en: the Americans all grew up reading books and watching movies where capturing an enemy flag was like a big deal.
sentences.zh: 美国人从小到大读的书和看的电影里，缴获敌人的旗帜都是一件了不起的大事。

sentences.en: But unbeknownst to them, there was this tradition in Japan.
sentences.zh: 但他们并不知道，日本有一种这样的传统。

sentences.en: And so everybody on the battlefield had a flag somewhere underneath them.
sentences.zh: 所以战场上的每个人，随身某处都藏着一面旗子。

sentences.en: servicemen just take all these flags back to the States.
sentences.zh: 军人把所有这些旗子都带回了美国。

sentences.en: But crucially, in the U.S., these good luck flags are not destroyed.
sentences.zh: 但关键在于，在美国，这些好运旗并没有被销毁。

sentences.en: Because they would just keep them and then they'd end up in your grandparents' attic or basement in Scranton or whatever.
sentences.zh: 因为他们会把它们留着，最后它们就会出现在斯克兰顿或其他地方你祖父母的阁楼或地下室里。

sentences.en: But this is where Rex and Keiko's Oban Society comes in.
sentences.zh: 但这就是雷克斯和惠子的御盘协会发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: Because what they do is they work with families in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的工作是与美国的家属合作，

sentences.en: who have come into possession of one of these good luck flags, and often as a form of post-war healing and reconciliation,
sentences.zh: 这些家属不知怎么就拥有了其中一面好运旗，通常作为战后疗伤和和解的一种形式，

sentences.en: they help them return the flag to the family of the original flag bearer in Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们帮助将旗帜归还给日本原旗帜持有者的家属。

sentences.en: Oh, so if you're like the grandson of a World War II veteran like me and find one of these flags in your grandfather's attic,
sentences.zh: 哦，所以如果你像我一样是个二战老兵的孙子，在爷爷的阁楼里发现了这样一面旗子，

sentences.en: the Oban Society will actually find the grandchildren of the Japanese veteran that they belong to, and then they will like matchmake and send them that flag.
sentences.zh: 御盘协会实际上会找到他们所属的日本老兵的孙辈，然后他们就会像牵红线一样把那面旗子寄过去。

sentences.en: And after starting out on their own more than a decade ago, Rex and Keiko say that today they have a team of about 14 people that specialize in sending back these flags.
sentences.zh: 在十多年前独立起步后，雷克斯和惠子说，如今他们拥有一个由大约 14 人组成的团队，专门负责寄回这些旗帜。

sentences.en: And it took us, I think, four years to do the first one, and now we're doing two each week on the average.
sentences.zh: 我想，我们花了四年时间才送回第一面，而现在我们平均每周能送回两面。

sentences.en: I mean, so then how many have they successfully returned at this point?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那么到目前为止他们成功归还了多少面？

sentences.en: Well, at this point, they gave me a rough estimate of about 400 total returns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，到目前为止，他们给我的粗略估计总共归还了大约 400 面。

sentences.en: And they say their success rate is, again, roughly speaking, maybe around 50%.
sentences.zh: 他们说他们的成功率，同样粗略地说，可能在 50% 左右。

sentences.en: Their fastest find was a few days.
sentences.zh: 他们最快的找寻只花了几天。

sentences.en: And then there are obviously ones that might take even longer, but they just don't know yet.
sentences.zh: 当然还有一些可能需要更长时间，但他们现在还不知道。

sentences.en: So you had mentioned that the biggest thing written on the flag was the name of the flag's owner.
sentences.zh: 所以你之前提到过，旗子上写得最多的东西是旗帜主人的名字。

sentences.en: Is that enough to find the descendants?
There are a lot of names that are the equivalent of, like, John Smith.
sentences.zh: 有很多名字相当于英语里的“约翰·史密斯”。

sentences.en: And so the only way to figure out which John Smith it belongs to is to figure out where it came from.
sentences.zh: 所以弄清楚它究竟属于哪个“约翰·史密斯”的唯一方法，就是弄清楚它是从哪里来的。

sentences.en: But something that is rarely seen on these flags is any geographical mention as to where it was created, which drives us nuts.
sentences.zh: 但这些旗子上极少能看到关于它是在哪里制作的地理提及，这把我们急疯了。

sentences.en: So if they write, they don't write the hometown's name.
sentences.zh: 所以如果他们写，他们不会写家乡的名字。

sentences.en: And then that's what we spend so many hours trying to figure out is where did this come from?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们花那么多时间试图弄清楚的地方：这究竟来自哪里？

sentences.en: So what are the techniques for figuring where they come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，弄清它们来自哪里的技术有哪些呢？

sentences.en: Well, they actually asked me not to divulge too much of their process because they don't want people who aren't experts when they find these flags to try to do this themselves.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们其实请我不要透露太多他们的流程，因为他们不希望不是专家的普通人在找到这些旗子时试图自己去做这件事。

sentences.en: I guess that makes sense, yeah.
And another thing I should add is that Rex and Keiko will never urge anyone to hand over a flag.
sentences.zh: 我还要补充一点，雷克斯和惠子绝不会敦促任何人交出旗子。

sentences.en: But you have to come to them.
And if instead you choose to keep it, they'll respect your decision no matter what it is.
sentences.zh: 如果你选择留着它，无论如何他们都会尊重你的决定。

sentences.en: You know, I think that this, like, flag return process sounds really heartfelt and great.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我觉得这个，呃，归还旗帜的过程听起来真的很走心，也很棒。

sentences.en: But it's also, you know, these flags are part of military campaigns that are extremely violent and not the best chapter in Japan's history.
sentences.zh: 但这也是，你知道的，这些旗子是极其暴力的军事行动的一部分，并非日本历史上最光彩的一章。

sentences.en: Are they ever used politically to, you know, hearken back in a bad way to this period of time where Japan's imperial strength was at its height?
sentences.zh: 它们有没有被政治化，用来，你知道的，以一种糟糕的方式回溯日本帝国力量达到顶峰的那个时期？

sentences.en: So I asked Rex and Keiko about that.
sentences.zh: 所以我问了雷克斯和惠子这个问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, they really stress that when it comes to these good luck flags, they've never found that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们真的强调，当谈到这些好运旗时，他们从来没有发现过这种情况。

sentences.en: What they've found is that the people they've worked with and returned these flags to in Japan really connect with them on a personal level.
sentences.zh: 他们发现的是，他们合作过并向其归还这些旗帜的日本民众，真的在个人层面上与它们建立了联系。

sentences.en: Because these are festooned, basically, with these messages and the names of these family members.
sentences.zh: 因为这些东西上面基本上缀满了这些信息和这些家庭成员的名字。

sentences.en: So much more than anything else, what it becomes is a memento from one single person's life.
sentences.zh: 比起其他任何东西，它更像是一个人一生的纪念品。

sentences.en: And this is what Keiko really stressed.
sentences.zh: 这也是惠子真正强调的。

sentences.en: Like, that was her big point.
When you read everything they are written, it is amazing.
sentences.zh: 当你阅读他们所写的一切时，这太神奇了。

sentences.en: So many stories you can learn and you can feel it from this spiritual object.
sentences.zh: 你可以了解到这么多的故事，并且能从这个精神物件中感受到它。

sentences.en: Because this is only one of the kind in the world.
sentences.zh: 因为这是世上独一无二的。

sentences.en: So do they end up connecting you with someone who either found or received a flag?
sentences.zh: 那他们最后会让你跟找到或收到旗子的人联系吗？

sentences.en: So I got a hold of Noriko Koishi via translator just outside the town of Kobe in Kyogo Prefecture.
sentences.zh: 因此，我通过翻译在兵库县神户市郊外联系到了石来典子。

sentences.en: Noriko is in her mid-80s, which means she really grew up during the war.
sentences.zh: 典子八十多岁了，这意味着她确实是在战争中长大的。

sentences.en: And back then, it was just her and her mother and her father, Noriatsu Yamaguchi.
sentences.zh: 那时，家里只有她、她母亲和她父亲山口宪笃。

sentences.en: And Noriatsu was an executive at a local ceramics factory.
sentences.zh: 宪笃是当地一家陶瓷厂的高管。

sentences.en: But Noriko says that her memories of him are very faint.
sentences.zh: 但典子说，她对父亲的记忆非常模糊。

sentences.en: Dad was a busy salaryman who worked very long hours.
sentences.zh: 爸爸是个大忙人，工作时间非常长。

sentences.en: So by the time she wakes up, he'll be already gone to work and then come back after she fell asleep.
sentences.zh: 所以等她醒来时，他已经去上班了，等她睡着后他才回来。

sentences.en: And obviously, because of the war, there is not much of a memory aside from that.
sentences.zh: 显然，因为战争，除了这些之外并没有留下太多记忆。

sentences.en: So instead, what she actually remembers most vividly about her father is him leaving for the war.
sentences.zh: 因此，她对父亲印象最深刻、最生动的反而是他去参军的那一幕。

sentences.en: Because when she was about nine years old, Noriatsu was drafted to go fight in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 因为在她九岁左右的时候，宪笃被征召去菲律宾作战。

sentences.en: And Noriko says he did not want to go.
Because, of course, by 1944, the whole country of Japan sort of knew that there won't be a victory.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，到了 1944 年，整个日本都隐约知道不会有胜利了。

sentences.en: But obviously, nobody is going to say that out loud.
sentences.zh: 但显然，没有人会大声说出来。

sentences.en: But the general thinking was that getting drafted at this point was basically a death sentence.
sentences.zh: 不过大家的普遍看法是，在这个时候被征召基本上就是判了死刑。

sentences.en: So Noriko actually remembers that her mother began kind of frantically suggesting that they all maybe run away to the countryside so that her father could dodge the draft.
sentences.zh: 所以典子确实记得，她母亲开始有点惊慌失措地建议他们全家也许可以逃到乡下去，这样她父亲就能逃避兵役。

sentences.en: So her grandfather was after him in the face, saying, the consequences of you doing that will result to they won't be able to get any food from the government.
sentences.zh: 所以她爷爷当面训斥他，说你这么做的后果会导致他们无法从政府那里得到任何食物。

sentences.en: Noriko won't be able to go to school.
It will be a disgrace to the family.
And she remembers that that scene where her grandfather hit her mother.
sentences.zh: 她还记得她爷爷打了她母亲的那一幕。

sentences.en: That is an incredibly intense thing to remember.
sentences.zh: 这是一件极其震撼且难以忘怀的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, and also just remembering the way they were kind of locked into this reality, which was that he had to go.
sentences.zh: 是的，还有那种记得他们被这种现实所困住的感觉，那就是他必须去。

sentences.en: And so her other vivid memory from that time is this kind of distilled image of the last moment she saw him.
sentences.zh: 所以她对那个时期的另一个生动记忆是，她最后一次见到他的那一刻的浓缩画面。

sentences.en: So she sent him off at the train station.
And her dad was sort of on the deck of the train.
sentences.zh: 她爸爸当时站在火车的月台上。

sentences.en: And he was wearing this white glove and waving at her until the train made that curve and she couldn't see him anymore.
sentences.zh: 他戴着白手套向她挥手，直到火车拐过那个弯，她再也看不见他。

sentences.en: And to this day, she still remembers that white glove in the distance waving at her.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，她依然记得远处那只向她挥手的白手套。

sentences.en: And then he just never came home.
sentences.zh: 然后他就再也没有回家。

sentences.en: And when Noriko was already 12 or 13, so well after the war ended, her mother finally received a letter in the mail from the government just saying,
sentences.zh: 当典子已经 12、13 岁时，也就是战争结束后很久，她的母亲终于在信箱里收到了一封来自政府的信，上面写着：

sentences.en: we can confirm he died in the war.
sentences.zh: 我们确认他在战争中阵亡了。

sentences.en: And they never received any remains.
sentences.zh: 他们从未收到任何遗体。

sentences.en: And so, since you're telling his story during this other story of good luck flags, presumably he was given a good luck flag.
sentences.zh: 既然你在讲述好运旗这个故事的同时讲述他的故事，想必他也曾被赠予过一面好运旗。

sentences.en: Did they know anything about that, the family?
sentences.zh: 家里人知道这方面的任何事情吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, so Noriko says that there had, in fact, been a sending off ceremony for her father, which she had attended, in which she put her handprint, actually,
sentences.zh: 是的，典子说，实际上曾为她父亲举行过一场欢送仪式，她也参加了，而且她甚至把自己的手印按在了

sentences.en: on a good luck flag that he took with him.
sentences.zh: 他随身携带的一面好运旗上。

sentences.en: But when I asked her if that ceremony meant anything to her at the time, or if she yearned to see the flag afterwards as the years went by, she was like, no.
sentences.zh: 但当我问她当时那个仪式对她意味着什么，或者随着岁月流逝，她是否渴望再次看到那面旗帜时，她的回答是：没有。

sentences.en: Obviously, they do so many flags when her uncles also went to war.
sentences.zh: 显然，当她的叔叔们也去参军时，他们做过太多面旗子了。

sentences.en: So, this was, you know, the 9th, 10th flag.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这是第 9 面、第 10 面旗子。

sentences.en: So, it became sort of a monotonous routine.
sentences.zh: 因此，这成了一种单调乏味的惯例。

sentences.en: She did not even think for a second about these flags.
sentences.zh: 她甚至没有哪怕一秒钟想起过这些旗帜。

sentences.en: I mean, I guess it makes sense when we talked about them being made over and over again for various people.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我们谈到这些旗子是一次又一次为不同的人制作时，这确实说得通。

sentences.en: Like, you do it, and, you know, life moves on, even if you face tragedy.
sentences.zh: 就像你做了它，然后，你知道的，生活还得继续，哪怕你面临着悲剧。

sentences.en: So, what I would like to hear at this point is that Noriko's good luck flag was found, and we have her little handprint on it.
sentences.zh: 所以，我此时最想听到的是典子的好运旗被找到了，上面还有她的小手印。

sentences.en: And who first found it, and how is itself a bit of a mystery?
sentences.zh: 是谁最先找到的，以及它是怎么被找到的本身就是一个谜。

sentences.en: Well, I actually didn't know anything.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我其实什么都不知道。

sentences.en: I really didn't know anything about his war experience.
sentences.zh: 我真的对他的战争经历一无所知。

sentences.en: I got a hold of her where she lives in Florida.
sentences.zh: 我在她位于佛罗里达州的住所联系到了她。

sentences.en: And the person she is talking about here is her late uncle, Neil Huard.
sentences.zh: 她在这里谈论的人是她已故的叔叔尼尔·霍华德。
也就是大家所知的巴德叔叔。

sentences.en: And Dionne, as a child growing up, spent vacations with her uncle and aunt in Michigan.
sentences.zh: 迪恩在童年成长过程中，曾在密歇根州与她的叔叔和阿姨一起度过假期。

sentences.en: And the two of them, they didn't have children, so they doted all over us.
sentences.zh: 他们两个没有孩子，所以对我们百般疼爱。

sentences.en: And they had a house that was on a lake, and he always had a boat ready for us.
sentences.zh: 他们有一栋湖畔别墅，他总是为我们备好一艘船。

sentences.en: I mean, he just wanted to play.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他只想陪我们玩。

sentences.en: But she also knew that he had served in the war in the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 但她也知道他曾在太平洋战场上服役。

sentences.en: And although she saw a lot of photos of him in uniform, what actually went on in the war was kind of like a no-go area.
sentences.zh: 尽管她看到了很多他穿着制服的照片，但战争中究竟发生了什么就像是一个禁区。

sentences.en: So, we have pictures of him in his uniform.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有他穿制服的照片。

sentences.en: We have pictures of him before he left.
sentences.zh: 我们有他离开前的照片。

sentences.en: We have pictures of him as they were training to leave, you know, yada-da-da.
sentences.zh: 我们有他们训练准备出发时的照片，你知道的，等等等等。

sentences.en: So, I knew from pictures something about it, but they never talked about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我从照片中了解了一些情况，但他们从不谈论此事。

sentences.en: This was not a discussion that you had at the house.
sentences.zh: 这不是你在家里会讨论的话题。

sentences.en: The only thing Dionne ever really learned, and even this was much later,
sentences.zh: 迪恩真正了解到的唯一一件事，而且甚至是在很久以后，

sentences.en: was that Uncle Bud had actually been found very badly wounded and in a coma on a battlefield before returning to the States.
sentences.zh: 那就是巴德叔叔在返回美国之前，曾被发现身受重伤且昏迷不醒地躺在战场上。

sentences.en: And that battlefield had been in the Philippines.
sentences.zh: 而那个战场就在菲律宾。

sentences.en: So, fast forward to the year 2016, when Uncle Bud, at the age of 95, passes away.
sentences.zh: 时间快进到 2016 年，95 岁高龄的巴德叔叔去世了。

sentences.en: And Dionne and the other family members are clearing out his things, including this crate of just, like, old stuff that no one else wants.
sentences.zh: 迪恩和其他家庭成员在清理他的遗物，其中包括一箱装着别人都不想要的旧玩意的板条箱。

sentences.en: So, I opened it up, and I pulled out this box.
sentences.zh: 所以，我把它打开，然后抽出了这个盒子。

sentences.en: And when she got back home and opened the box,
sentences.zh: 当她回到家里打开盒子时，

sentences.en: there was this white bag with this silk material in it.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个白色袋子，装着丝绸材质的东西。

sentences.en: And I was like, what the heck is this?
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，这到底是什么鬼？

sentences.en: And although she didn't know it at the time,
what it was, was a good luck flag.
And here, let me show it to you.

sentences.zh: 哇，它看起来跟新的一样。

sentences.en: It's, like, not faded at all.
So, as you set this up,
sentences.zh: 所以，当你们摆出这面旗时，

sentences.en: I'm expecting this to be Noriko's father's flag,
sentences.zh: 我以为这是典子父亲的旗帜，

sentences.en: but there's no handprint on it.
Here is where there is a tiny little twist in the story.
sentences.zh: 故事在这里有了一个小小的转折。

sentences.en: Because Dionne, after doing some Googling,
sentences.zh: 因为戴安在谷歌上搜索了一番后，

sentences.en: figured out what kind of flag it was.
And she decided that she wanted to find the flag's original family.
sentences.zh: 她决定要找到这面旗帜最初的家人。

sentences.en: And so she sent it to Rex and Keiko,
sentences.zh: 于是她把它寄给了雷克斯和惠子，
然后他们开始进行分析。

sentences.en: And so, looking back at the flag,
sentences.zh: 所以，回过头来看这面旗帜，

sentences.en: do you see the characters along the right-hand edge,
sentences.zh: 你看到右边缘的那些字了吗，

sentences.en: So that is the name of a ceramics factory
sentences.zh: 那是日本兵库县神户市

sentences.en: in the town of Kobe in Hyogo Prefecture, Japan.
So this is, this was from his factory where he worked.
sentences.zh: 所以这是，这是他工作工厂的东西。

sentences.en: This is, like, a flag from his co-worker sending him off.
sentences.zh: 这就像是他同事送他出征的旗帜。

sentences.en: Yeah, he had a second flag, and this was it.
sentences.zh: 对，他有第二面旗，就是这面。

sentences.en: So after telling Dionne, you know, hey, it could take years,
sentences.zh: 所以，在告诉戴安“你知道的，这可能需要几年时间”之后，

sentences.en: Rex and Keiko called her, like, two months later.
sentences.zh: 雷克斯和惠子大约两个月后就给戴安打了个电话。

sentences.en: And said, we found the family.
And I was like, you're kidding.
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，你在开玩笑吧。

sentences.en: And they said, no, we're not.
sentences.zh: 他们说，不，我们没开玩笑。

sentences.en: And it was at this point that Dionne says
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，戴安说

sentences.en: she did start to have some trepidation

sentences.zh: 产生了一些忐忑不安的感觉。

sentences.en: Because having already handed over the flag
sentences.zh: 因为既然已经把旗帜交给了

sentences.en: to Oban Society, there were no takebacks.
sentences.zh: 御盆会，就没有反悔的余地了。

sentences.en: She couldn't ask for it back.
And so now that they'd found the family,
sentences.zh: 所以现在他们找到了那家人，

sentences.en: Dionne says this thing she had set in motion
sentences.zh: 戴安说她这一系列举动

sentences.en: And she was getting kind of nervous.
And part of the reason was, is I really wasn't sure
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于，我真的不确定

sentences.en: what the rest of my family would think about this, right?
sentences.zh: 我的家人会怎么看待这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: I was making this executive decision.
Is that because you didn't tell anyone else
